CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's Q1 2026 results were undeniably strong: revenue up 22.2% YoY to $17.4B, EPS of $5.47 (adjusted $5.54) beating consensus by 19%, and a record $63B backlog providing multi-year visibility. The AI data center power generation theme is a genuine secular tailwind, with Energy & Transportation segment sales up 22% and management tripling large engine capacity targets. However, the stock has already re-rated massively — P/E has expanded from ~16.6x a year ago to ~42.8x today, and P/B from 9.1x to 21.6x — pricing in much of this good news. Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B for 2026 are compressing margins (operating margin 17.7% vs. prior year, Resource Industries margin collapsed to 10% from 17%), and the QoQ revenue actually declined 1.3%. Operating cash flow was only $1.87B in Q1 vs. $3.74B in Q3, and the $5.7B shareholder return in Q1 (including $5B buyback) consumed cash. The stock at $866 is near all-time highs after a 170% surge over 12 months, leaving limited margin of safety. The fundamental trajectory is positive but the valuation now demands flawless execution on a cyclical business facing real tariff and macro headwinds (rising bond yields, weak China data, oil at $100). Mildly attractive on balance — good business, stretched price.
